title: 0-10 V voltage signals
summary: 0-10 V signals are simple and common for setpoints and short cable runs, but they have no live zero and are more sensitive to voltage drops and noise than current loops.

sections.heading: Use cases
sections.body: Voltage signals are typical for drive speed setpoints, potentiometers and sensors inside the control cabinet. The input has a high impedance, so it does not load the source.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.body: A broken wire reads as 0 V, which is indistinguishable from a real zero. Long cables and shared ground paths add errors. For field transmitters, 4-20 mA is usually preferred.

sections.heading: Wrong type on a channel
sections.body: Connecting a current loop to a voltage input or the reverse produces nonsense: a current transmitter on a high-impedance voltage input drives the input towards the loop supply voltage. In PLC Lab this is simulated: configure the channel type to match the device.
